paragraphs: Here's the big idea, baker: God keeps His promises, right on time. Simeon was told by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ (Luke 2:26), and then he walked into the temple courts just as Mary and Joseph carried that Child in (Luke 2:27). Simeon said, "my eyes have seen Your salvation" (Luke 2:30). I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS thinking I'd been forgotten, and I can tell you the waiting was never the end of the story.

Look at who gets the good news, friend. Simeon calls this salvation "a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to Your people Israel" (Luke 2:32). Anna, a prophetess who never left the temple, gave thanks to God and spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem (Luke 2:37-38). Jesus is for ALL people, because this salvation is prepared "in the sight of all people" (Luke 2:31).

Simeon also tells Mary the truth that this Child is "a sign that will be spoken against" and that "a sword will pierce your soul as well" (Luke 2:34-35). I think that's a heavy word for a mother to hear. Still, the passage ends with the Child growing strong, filled with wisdom, with "the grace of God" upon Him (Luke 2:40). So keep waiting, keep praying, and keep your ovens ready, because God knows what He's doing. The story isn't over, baker, and neither is the teaching.
